title: Go: Context Package
description: Master Go's context package for cancellation, timeouts, and passing request-scoped values.

steps.title: context.Background
steps.description: Create a background context with `context.Background()`. Print its type and deadline using `ctx.Deadline()` (should be zero time, false).
hints: It is the root of any context tree
`ctx.Deadline()` returns `(time.Time, bool)` — the bool is false for Background

verification.failureMessage: Print the result of ctx.Deadline() to show no deadline.

steps.title: WithCancel
steps.description: Create a cancellable context with `context.WithCancel(ctx)`. Launch a goroutine that checks `ctx.Done()` and prints "Cancelled!" when cancelled. Call `cancel()` from main and print "Main exiting".
hints: Always defer cancel() to release resources

verification.failureMessage: Use ctx.Done() channel in a select inside the goroutine.

steps.title: WithTimeout
steps.description: Use `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 100*time.Millisecond)` to create a context that auto-cancels after 100ms. Print "Timed out!" when the context expires.
hints: Don't forget to defer cancel() to avoid resource leaks
The context's Done channel fires automatically after the duration

verification.failureMessage: Wait on ctx.Done() in a select to detect timeout.

steps.title: WithValue
steps.description: Use `context.WithValue(ctx, "user", "Alice")` to store a value. In a function `process(ctx context.Context)`, retrieve it with `ctx.Value("user")` and print the result passed to the process function.
hints: `context.WithValue(ctx, key, val)` returns a derived context

verification.failureMessage: Use type assertion to convert the value from ctx.Value.

steps.title: Context in HTTP handler
steps.description: Write an HTTP handler that creates a context with timeout, simulates work with a slow operation, and returns "Completed" on success or "Request cancelled" on timeout. Listen on :8081.
hints: Use `r.Context()` to get the request's context
Use a select to race between work done and ctx.Done()

verification.failureMessage: Use r.Context() to get the request context.
